report.diff: --- /dev/null +++ b/tests/test_regression_nested_match_previous.py @@ -0,0 +1,48 @@ +import pyparsing as pp + + +def test_match_previous_expr_nested_different_tags(): + # SO https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78574784/ - nested open/close tags + # opener name and closer must match, LIFO for nesting: + # ... should parse, ... should not + tag_open_name = pp.Word(pp.alphas) + tag_close_name = pp.match_previous_expr(tag_open_name) + + open_tag = "<" + tag_open_name + ">" + close_tag = "" + + element = pp.Forward() + element <<= pp.Group( + open_tag + pp.ZeroOrMore(element | pp.Word(pp.alphas)) + close_tag + ) + + # single level sanity is covered by nested case; nested with distinct + # tags must succeed + result = element.parse_string("hello", parse_all=True) + # verify structure contains both tags + flat = " ".join(result.as_list()[0][:5]) + assert "a" in flat and "b" in flat + + +def test_match_previous_expr_nested_mismatch_detected(): + tag_open_name = pp.Word(pp.alphas) + tag_close_name = pp.match_previous_expr(tag_open_name) + + open_tag = "<" + tag_open_name + ">" + close_tag = "" + + element = pp.Forward() + element <<= pp.Group( + open_tag + pp.ZeroOrMore(element | pp.Word(pp.alphas)) + close_tag + ) + + # mismatched nesting must raise, not silently succeed + try: + element.parse_string("hello", parse_all=True) + except pp.ParseBaseException: + pass + else: + raise AssertionError("mismatched nested tags should not parse") + + # correctly nested must succeed + element.parse_string("hello", parse_all=True)
